Each GitHub issue will include:

- Detailed acceptance criteria covering happy paths, boundaries, failures, accessibility, security, and tests

- Persistence, concurrency, idempotency, and ownership expectations where applicable

For example, ticket 9 would not merely say “explore repayment scenarios.” Its acceptance criteria would specify that:

- Additional repayments retain every existing repayment and subtract the proposed amount exactly once.
- Changed repayments remove only the selected existing commitment and add the replacement exactly once.
- Switching modes recalculates from the immutable basis snapshot and clears incompatible values.
- Accessible savings and the protected reserve never become monthly repayment capacity.
- Exact zero, one-penny shortfall, protected-buffer equality, and one-penny buffer misses have deterministic outcomes.
- The result uses only the approved qualified phrases.
- No repayment amount is recommended.
- Previewing a scenario never mutates the financial statement or basis snapshot.
- Exact source totals, formula, limitations, warnings, and support routes remain inspectable.
- Keyboard operation, status announcements, input preservation, and responsive layouts are verified.
- Domain and browser tests use independently worked expected values.

## What to build

Deliver the first complete tracer bullet of Customer Financial Health.
A reviewer starts the system with Docker Compose, opens the React application, and sees a seeded fictional customer's current monthly position loaded through FastAPI from PostgreSQL.
The result must be calculated by the pure deterministic financial-health module rather than by the browser, HTTP handler, database, or Azure OpenAI.

The slice includes the minimum application structure needed to keep later work modular: a React and TypeScript frontend, a FastAPI modular monolith, PostgreSQL persistence, an explicit one-shot migration process, generated TypeScript API access, and independently testable domain logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One documented Docker Compose command starts the frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, and migration workflow from a clean checkout.
- [ ] Startup succeeds when all Azure OpenAI settings are absent.
- [ ] The database is migrated and seeded idempotently with one fictional customer and one confirmed snapshot.
- [ ] The browser overview obtains the snapshot through the real generated client and FastAPI workflow endpoint rather than bundled frontend fixture data.
- [ ] The overview leads with normalized monthly income, normalized monthly outgoings, and exact monthly headroom in GBP using calm, qualified language.
- [ ] The customer can inspect original amounts, original frequencies, normalized monthly values, source totals, the subtraction formula, calculation-policy version, and information limitations.
- [ ] Weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual frequencies follow the versioned normalization policy.
- [ ] All backend money arithmetic uses decimal values and all persisted money uses fixed precision.
- [ ] A positive balance is never presented as proof of long-term affordability or as an approval.
- [ ] Result meaning is communicated with text and exact amounts rather than color alone.
- [ ] The FastAPI liveness endpoint reports process health.
- [ ] The readiness endpoint verifies PostgreSQL connectivity and compatible migrations while treating Azure OpenAI as optional.
- [ ] The frontend presents a recoverable loading or unavailable state if it starts before the backend.

## Required verification

- [ ] Independent worked examples verify frequency normalization, source totals, and monthly headroom through the public financial-health interface.
- [ ] A PostgreSQL integration test proves the stored decimal values and seeded snapshot can be read through the repository seam.
- [ ] An API contract test proves the overview response is closed and contains no client-supplied calculated or authority-bearing fields.
- [ ] A browser test proves the visible seeded values arrived through the running frontend, API, and database.
- [ ] A clean-start smoke test proves migrations, seed idempotency, health checks, and operation without Azure credentials.

## Guardrails and exclusions

- Azure OpenAI must not calculate money, select a result, choose warnings, or affect readiness.
- Production authentication, generic table CRUD, queues, microservices, GraphQL, and public deployment are outside this slice.
- Do not claim a run or test command in documentation until it has been exercised.

- [ ] Accessible savings and protected reserve are non-negative, while an overdraft is represented explicitly as a negative current-account balance rather than negative savings.
- [ ] Savings above protected reserve is calculated as the greater of zero and accessible savings minus protected reserve.
- [ ] A reserve gap is displayed separately when the protected reserve exceeds accessible savings.
- [ ] Accessible savings never become recurring income and never erase a monthly shortfall.
- [ ] Known arrears remain separate from recurring outgoings and existing repayment commitments.
- [ ] Missing resilience information does not block the current-position result and produces a specific limitation.
- [ ] Below, equal-to, and above-reserve boundaries have deterministic resilience results.
- [ ] A positive monthly position with weak resilience and a monthly shortfall with substantial savings are both described as mixed pictures rather than collapsed into one score.
- [ ] The overview exposes the values and formula behind the resilience result.

## Required verification

- [ ] Domain examples cover savings below, equal to, and above the reserve, a reserve gap, a negative current-account balance, and a monthly shortfall with savings.
- [ ] API and persistence tests prove original resilience values and calculated outputs retain decimal precision and customer ownership.
- [ ] A browser test proves resilience is visible but optional and does not alter the displayed monthly headroom.
- [ ] Component checks verify long currency values and negative balance formatting do not overlap or use scientific notation.

From the repository root:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

You do not currently need to copy `.env.example`. Compose reads it directly.

Open:

- Backend readiness: [http://localhost:8000/health/ready](http://localhost:8000/health/ready)

To run in the background:

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
docker compose ps
```

To inspect logs:

```bash
docker compose logs -f
```

Or inspect one service:

```bash
docker compose logs -f backend
docker compose logs -f migrate
docker compose logs -f frontend
docker compose logs -f db
```

Stop containers while preserving database data:

```bash
docker compose down
```

Reset the fictional database completely:

```bash
docker compose down -v
docker compose up --build
```

The `-v` command deletes the local PostgreSQL volume and cannot recover its contents.

```bash
docker run -d --name cfha-test-postgres \

  -e POSTGRES_DB=customer_financial_health_test \
  -p 55432:5432 \

cd backend
uv run pytest
```

```bash
cd frontend
npm ci
npm run test
npm run lint
npx tsc -b --noEmit
```

Regenerate the API contract after backend schema changes:

```bash
cd backend
PYTHONPATH=src uv run export-openapi
```

#!/bin/sh

set -eu

script_directory=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
repository_directory=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$script_directory/.." && pwd)
compose_project=${SMOKE_COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-cfha-clean-smoke}
backend_port=${SMOKE_BACKEND_PORT:-18001}
frontend_port=${SMOKE_FRONTEND_PORT:-15174}
temporary_directory=$(mktemp -d)

compose() {
  docker compose \
    --project-name "$compose_project" \
    --file "$repository_directory/docker-compose.yml" \
    --file "$repository_directory/docker-compose.e2e.yml" \
    "$@"
}

cleanup() {
  compose down --volumes --remove-orphans
  rm -rf "$temporary_directory"
}

fail() {
  echo "Clean-environment smoke failed: $1" >&2
  exit 1
}

trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM

cleanup

BACKEND_PORT="$backend_port" FRONTEND_PORT="$frontend_port" \
  compose up --build --detach --wait

ready_url="http://localhost:$backend_port/health/ready"
live_url="http://localhost:$backend_port/health/live"
overview_url="http://localhost:$backend_port/overview"

curl -fsS "$live_url" | grep -q '"status":"ok"' || fail "liveness did not report ok"
curl -fsS "$ready_url" > "$temporary_directory/ready.json"
grep -q '"status":"ready"' "$temporary_directory/ready.json" || fail "readiness did not report ready"
grep -q '"database":"ok"' "$temporary_directory/ready.json" || fail "database was not ready"
grep -q '"classification_suggestions":"not_configured"' "$temporary_directory/ready.json" || fail "classification unexpectedly requires Azure"
grep -q '"personalized_guidance":"not_configured"' "$temporary_directory/ready.json" || fail "guidance unexpectedly requires Azure"

curl -fsS "$overview_url" > "$temporary_directory/overview-before.json"
compose run --rm migrate
curl -fsS "$overview_url" > "$temporary_directory/overview-after-seed.json"
cmp "$temporary_directory/overview-before.json" "$temporary_directory/overview-after-seed.json" >/dev/null || fail "idempotent seed changed the fictional aggregate"

compose restart db
BACKEND_PORT="$backend_port" FRONTEND_PORT="$frontend_port" compose up --detach --wait backend
curl -fsS "$overview_url" > "$temporary_directory/overview-after-restart.json"
cmp "$temporary_directory/overview-before.json" "$temporary_directory/overview-after-restart.json" >/dev/null || fail "restart did not preserve stored data"

compose exec -T db psql -U financial_health -d financial_health \
  -c "update alembic_version set version_num = 'reviewer_schema_mismatch'" >/dev/null

status=$(curl -sS -o "$temporary_directory/mismatch.json" -w '%{http_code}' "$ready_url")
[ "$status" = "503" ] || fail "schema mismatch did not make readiness return 503"
